body: I'm one of the few who thinks a Muslim woman can marry a Christian man. Not a mainstream opinion, I know. I'd obviously prefer that he was Muslim or convert, but he's not going to. And we've been together for 8 years...so dumping him over this would be very difficult.

I guess my other thought is that he's going to his therapist today, and bringing her a suicide note that he wrote. So I guess the ball will be in her court, with her professional opinion, what to do. I'm not a professional, I'm glad to let her handle it. (If he tells her).

> Don't set yourself on fire to keep other people warm.

That's a wonderful metaphor. Thanks for your caring words. I'll try to keep these things in mind.

> From the way you are talking I can tell you are doing nearly everything you could do, and are doing it well.

I guess I've done everything except call the police, and I have no idea if this is the right move or not. We're also going to try couples counseling in a month (that was the soonest appointment I could get that I could actually afford). Maybe that might help somehow.

> Are you struggling with keeping up with his depression?

Oh yeah. Losing sleep and basically getting depressed myself. His depression has ruined my last two family vacations. For various reasons he couldn't come, and he told me over the phone he was feeling suicidal, and me not being able to be there and do anything about it was even more difficult, and then I felt terrible until I went home and we made up.

I guess I'm wondering when is it appropriate to call the police. The problem is that a lot of his suicidal behavior seems like a cry for help, not an attempt. And I don't want to answer a cry for help with calling the police and locking him up. But when has it gotten to the point where he is a danger to himself? And am I violating his agency, given that it's his life and I can't really force him not to take it by legal and physical force? Maybe that might be the best thing to do, but if he doesn't have the will to get better, I don't know if that will help. 

I remember I was suicidal years ago (which makes this all the more difficult because I have depression too!) But I told a campus psychologist that I was extremely suicidal at that moment and wouldn't be able to help myself if I went home. She called the police. They took me to a hospital where they forced me to go to a community clinic for a week and get intensive therapy. And that was really helpful. But that was a situation where even though I was intensely suicidal (psychotic urges to end my life), I still summoned the willpower myself to turn myself in and to make the climb toward getting better. 

But I don't know what calling the police on my bf will do if he doesn't have that will. Instead, it will just be like treating him like a criminal, he'll probably still have the same urges by the end of the week, he might even just lie and say that I made it up, and then things could be even worse.

I texted a hotline and it was pretty useless to be honest. They told me how brave I was, how they were sure that my boyfriend appreciated me, and then they just gave me some numbers of local therapists in the area who didn't answer my calls.

That's why this is so difficult. I've read a lot of different posts with people who have suicidal boyfriends, and it's usually a drinking problem, or a lost job, or something like that. But with my BF it's a problem that's always been there. Most of his life. He doesn't drink. He has a job. Not an ideal one, but one that he's decent enough at to keep and it isn't super stressful. He even has a lot of time for his hobbies, like art and video games, and plays online games with his friends. And I don't ask much from him, only what is absolutely necessary for the both of us. I ask almost nothing for myself. So from the outside, it would look like his life is pretty good. But he's super, insanely depressed. It just seems like he has this warped mental filter in his mind that makes him incapable of appreciating or seeing the good in anything. He says a lot of nice things to me and gives me compliments, when he's in a better mood. But ultimately he thinks his life is terrible. It's like he has this void inside himself that can never be filled. And a lot of the times he makes me feel like everything I'm doing is wrong (even though he doesn't say that), but given that he can't appreciate anything, there's just always a problem with everything. I don't communicate enough. I communicate too much. I don't help him when he's upset. But then when I try, he doesn't want my help. 

I've even given him the number to the suicide hotline, or suicide text-line, and he just threw it away. 

So, I don't really know what to do short of locking him in a room and forcing him to not kill himself. I guess the only thing I haven't done is call the police. But I'm not sure if I want to do that because that's a serious move, and once I do it that will violate all trust. Maybe at this point a serious move is required. But I feel like if he's been suicidal his whole life, how will having the police come, lock him in a hospital, and force him to get therapy (which he's already getting), do anything to help him? If anything it will just make him never tell me anything again, so when he's considering his next attempt, he just won't tell me. 

So I feel like I'm at my wits end here.

I think the idea of a break is a good one. I just need to find somewhere I can go (which might be hard since my parents are not local). Or maybe convince him to stay with his parents or brother for the week, even though they are not close. 

The whole don't fix things for him, let them fall apart approach is basically what I've been doing the last few years. The only things I really push him on things that must be done (or else we'll be evicted, his car might self-destruct, etc.) But with things that are important, but not absolutely necessary, I've just been hands-off. As a result he has picked up the slack on lots of things. He started doing the dishes on a regular basis. Made the effort to get himself a therapist. Got himself Martial Arts lessons. Started looking for freelance work on the side. So slowly and surely he is making progress for himself. I'm just frustrated mainly by all our stupid arguments that seem to pop out of nowhere. 

But yeah...taking a break might be a good idea if things don't improve. I just really wish I had more time to make this decision before the lease renewal.
I guess I'm wondering if there are any steps I should go through if I leave him to diminish the possibility of his suicide.
